review_notes: I read the whole test file and the definitions and lemmas it relies on in Surreal/ZFC/OmnificCodes.lean (Divides, IsUnit, IsIrreducible, IsPrime, their *_iff bridge lemmas, and the value_zero, value_one and value_mul simp lemmas). I grepped for other uses of the *_iff lemmas: 14 hits in OmnificCodes.lean, 2 in Primality/ZFC.lean, 6 in this file. Everything else in the target is a term-mode restatement of an exported theorem, with no simp involvement. I could not run Lean. The suggestion rests on reading the definitions: Divides, IsUnit, IsIrreducible and IsPrime are plain, non-reducible defs, so simp cannot see through them. I did not check whether the extra simp lemmas would clash with a lemma elsewhere in the project. Confidence is moderate because the missing simp attributes may be intentional.

findings.declaration: Tests.ZFC examples using simp [OmnificCode.isPrime_iff / isIrreducible_iff / isUnit_iff / divides_iff] (pattern across five examples)
findings.problem: OmnificCode.Divides, IsUnit, IsIrreducible and IsPrime are opaque defs. Their bridge lemmas to the ring predicates (divides_iff, isUnit_iff, isIrreducible_iff, isPrime_iff) are not tagged @[simp], although the related value_zero, value_one and value_mul are. So every simp call about these predicates must name the matching bridge lemma by hand. The five examples at lines 43–56 do exactly that, and they are the only simp uses of these lemmas outside the lemma file. The canonical normal form is clear and terminating: code predicates rewrite to the ring predicates on `x.value`, and the existing `value_zero`/`value_one`/`value_mul` simp lemmas then normalise the argument. The interface is therefore incomplete as it stands.
findings.proposed_change: In OmnificCodes.lean, mark `divides_iff`, `isUnit_iff`, `isIrreducible_iff` and `isPrime_iff` with `@[simp]`, oriented as they are (code predicate ↔ predicate on `x.value`). Then reduce the examples to plain `simp`, for instance `example : ¬(0 : OmnificCode.{u}).IsPrime := by simp`. If tagging them globally is judged too aggressive, add dedicated simp lemmas for the degenerate cases, such as `not_isPrime_zero`, `not_isIrreducible_one`, `isUnit_one`, `divides_zero_zero` and `not_divides_zero_one`. Alternatively, keep the bridge lemmas non-simp and say so in their docstrings.
findings.benefit: Users reasoning about omnific codes get the ring-theoretic normal form from `simp` without knowing which of the four bridge lemmas to list. The test file would also check the real simp interface, since its examples currently pass the lemmas explicitly and so cannot detect a gap in the simp set.

evidence.excerpt: theorem isPrime_iff (x : OmnificCode.{u}) : x.IsPrime ↔ Prime x.value
theorem divides_iff (x y : OmnificCode.{u}) : Divides x y ↔ x.value ∣ y.value
